fluff.overview: The Vigilant-class corvette was one of the earliest WarShip designs produced by the Terran Hegemony, entering service in 2320 during the turbulent early years of the Age of War. Constructed by Dekirk Aerospace at their Graham IV facilities, the Vigilant was designed as a reconnaissance and surveillance platform built around a compact Kearny-Fuchida drive. The class emphasized speed and endurance over raw combat power, and its generous cargo holds and troop accommodation made it well suited to extended independent patrols along remote trade routes and contested borders. Though lightly armed and thinly armored for a vessel of its era, the Vigilant earned a reputation for reliability and remarkable longevity, with surplus examples remaining in active fleet rosters across multiple successor states centuries after the original production run ended.
fluff.capabilities:
At 140,000 tons and 266 meters, the Vigilant is a compact corvette armed with a diverse but light weapons suite spread across multiple arcs. A single White Shark capital missile launcher in the nose provides the heaviest forward punch, while five NAC/10 naval autocannons are distributed across the forward quarters, broadsides, and aft arc, giving the ship omnidirectional capital-grade firepower despite the modest caliber. The broadsides add paired large lasers for anti-fighter defense, the aft quarters carry White Shark launchers and paired PPCs, and three conventional AC/10 autocannons in the direct aft arc provide a final deterrent against pursuit. Eight hundred single heat sinks manage the thermal load.

Despite this respectable spread of weapons, the Vigilant suffered from targeting and tracking system limitations that hindered effective fire coordination, making it vulnerable against determined opposition. Only 88 tons of standard armor protect the hull, a thin margin for a vessel expected to operate independently on long patrols. A single 30-meter gravity deck supports the crew on extended deployments. Six aerospace fighters and four small craft provide organic screening capability, while the eighty-four-marine complement enables boarding operations and intelligence asset recovery.
fluff.deployment:
Three Federated Suns Vigilants, the FSS Point Barrow, FSS Smolensk, and FSS Batavia, all originally Hegemony vessels, participated in the Malagrotta Affair of 2573. Responding to distress calls from miners, the Federated Suns squadron engaged a Taurian Concordat force at a Lagrange jump point and destroyed or captured all but one Taurian vessel, losing only a single Leopard CV-class DropShip.

The FWLS Samhain served in the Free Worlds League Navy during the First Succession War, deployed to the Corey system in September 2787 as part of an escort group that included destroyers and a battleship. When Capellan forces led by the Congress-class frigate Tianjin attacked, the Samhain and her escorts destroyed two enemy WarShips before being overwhelmed.

Among the last of the class, the DCS Wyrm served the Draconis Combine as part of the nadir jump point blockade during the 2853 assault on Hesperus II. The Wyrm was destroyed on 25 October 2853 when the Lyran Commonwealth reactivated the ancient battlecruiser LCS Invincible, which smashed through the blockade fleet.
fluff.history:
The Vigilant-class corvette was born in the chaotic early Age of War, entering Hegemony service in 2320 as a reconnaissance and surveillance platform designed to complement the slightly older Bonaventure class. Dekirk Aerospace at Graham IV built the Vigilant around a compact Kearny-Fuchida drive, emphasizing speed and endurance over combat power. Crews typically deployed in mixed squadrons with Bonaventures, conducting intelligence-gathering sweeps along trade routes and contested borders that they informally called naughty picture runs.

The Vigilant served the Hegemony through the turbulent decades of the Age of War, including the Capellan Confederation's invasion of Terra Firma in 2409 where Vigilants were among the responding forces. By 2432, however, the design was officially replaced by the newer Vincent Mk.39-class corvette. Rather than scrapping the surplus hulls, the Hegemony sold them to neighboring Great Houses, giving the class a second life that would last centuries. The Federated Suns acquired a substantial number, deploying at least ten Vigilants during the Reunification War era. In 2573, three of them participated in the Malagrotta Affair, engaging and defeating a Taurian Concordat squadron. Other Great Houses fielded Vigilants in border patrol and convoy escort roles throughout this period, taking advantage of the low acquisition cost of surplus Hegemony hulls.

By 2765, the Rim Worlds Republic had amassed the largest fleet of Vigilants with thirty vessels, dwarfing every other operator. The Lyran Commonwealth maintained four, the Capellan Confederation three, and the Federated Suns still operated a sizable contingent. None accompanied Operation EXODUS, leaving only Successor State examples to soldier on through the Succession Wars. The absence of any Clan examples meant the class had no path to preservation through the advanced refit programs that extended the lives of other Star League-era designs.

Attrition during the Succession Wars steadily reduced the remaining Vigilant fleet. A corvette with known fire-control limitations and thin armor fared poorly in the brutal fleet actions that consumed WarShip after WarShip across the First and Second Succession Wars, and each loss was irreplaceable with no shipyard capable of laying down new keels. Vessels were expended in engagements where their light broadside offered little against heavier combatants, and the few that survived did so largely by avoiding pitched battle. The last confirmed examples were destroyed during a fleet action at Hesperus II in 2853, bringing to an end a class that had served for over five centuries.
